transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: fw-2026-05-04-0b9f3a7d
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Alicia, Miguel, Liam, Nora (CobaltWorks)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding runways for CobaltWorks' platform integration with Redwood. Focus areas: VPC peering / networking, staging environment access, API gateway routing and auth, security/compliance checks (SOC2/SSO/K M S), and pilot scope for latency/cost targets. Agreed to run a staging benchmark and share network checklist + security artifacts.

Topics covered:
- Production vs staging topology and who owns what for egress/ingress
- API gateway patterns and token routing for multi-tenant vs single-tenant workloads
- Data residency & encryption (K M S) and log retention needs
- Timeline for pilot and success metrics (p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens)

Action items called out in call (see metadata): Priya to send runbook + connectivity checklist; Marcus to book benchmark; Jordan attach SOC2 docs to CRM; CobaltWorks to send SSO metadata and sample traffic.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Priya from Redwood, and with me is Marcus our solutions engineer and Jordan who's going to help run the activation. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Alicia Park: good, thanks. we've got a couple folks here from infra and security, wanted to make sure we align on network and compliance first.
[00:20] Miguel Santos: yeah, hi, miguel here, devops. main ask is we need predictable staging access so our platform tests the traffic shaping before we flip prod traffic.
[00:30] Marcus Li: perfect. so today I'd like to map out the staging touchpoints — who runs the gateway, what auth we use, and how we handle prefix caching and KV cache warmup.
[00:42] Nora Chen: sorry can you repeat that last bit? prefix what?
[00:44] Marcus Li: oh yeah, prefix caching — like prefix/K V cache — small typo; it's the part of the runtime that caches repeated context so you don't re-send tokens for the same warmup.
[00:58] Liam O'Connor: Liam (security). couple quick items: SOC two is table stakes, we also need audit logs, S S O / Saml metadata, and confirmation around K M S integration for key rotation.
[01:12] Priya Patel: absolutely, we'll share SOC2 and the runbook. note: Redwood Dedicated is an option if you want predictable throughput — sorry that was "Redwood Dedicaed" in my notes — but we can scope dedicated vs hosted depending on traffic.
[01:27] Alicia Park: on dedicated, can you explain the network patterns? we want to avoid routing customer data through third-party networks.
[01:35] Marcus Li: yes, with Dedicated you can have reserved pools and VPC peering; traffic stays in your VPC for egress, and we support private endpoints. for private deployments we also offer a customer-managed control plane in case you need an air-gapped option.
[01:52] Miguel Santos: ok, who configures the peering? us or Redwood?
[01:55] Jordan Nguyen: typically it's a joint effort — we provide a VPC connectivity checklist and the terraform snippets; you'll run the peering on your side and we'll validate the routes. we'll send the checklist after this call.
[02:07] Miguel Santos: perfect. also need to know which ports and IP ranges to open.
[02:10] Marcus Li: we'll include that. note that for streaming outputs you want lower latency paths so we'll highlight the egress S N A P — sorry that was an auto-text — egress endpoints, and the NAT considerations.
[02:25] Nora Chen: about staging: can we mirror production traffic distribution? we want to run timed burst tests to see queueing behavior.
[02:33] Priya Patel: yes, that's part of the staging benchmark. Marcus will run a baseline on your sample prompt set to capture p50/p95/p99 and we'll also estimate token unit cost for both hosted and dedicated configs.
[02:45] Marcus Li: quick note — if your sequence lengths are high, we suggest quantization-friendly model variants and batching settings. batching helps with cost but can affect tail latency.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: quantization — just checking, does Redwood manage the keys or integrate with our K M S? we use HashiCorp Vault for keys.
[03:06] Marcus Li: we integrate with external K M S / H S M — HashiCorp is supported; we'll ask for the contact and configuration details.
[03:14] Alicia Park: about logs and retention — our compliance needs 12 months of audit logs. can Redwood ship logs to our SIEM?
[03:21] Jordan Nguyen: yes, we can forward audit logs via S3 or syslog; we'll attach the agent configs. also we have per-route metrics in the console you can export.
[03:33] Miguel Santos: how do secrets surface to the app? do tokens ever get logged?
[03:36] Marcus Li: tokens are redacted by default in our logs; full requests can be forwarded only if you enable it, but we'd rather use pointer references and K V cache references to avoid logging PII.
[03:48] Priya Patel: can I pause and align on timeline? what's your desired pilot window?
[03:52] Alicia Park: we'd like to start a 4-week pilot as soon as networking is done. goal is to validate latency under prod-like bursts and confirm cost targets.
[04:02] Priya Patel: great. recommended runway: 1 week for infra/connectivity, 1 week to provision staging and seeds, 2 weeks for benchmarks and iteration. does that work?
[04:13] Nora Chen: yes, that aligns.
[04:15] Marcus Li: for the benchmark session I'd ask to have a dedicated environment with about 10k tokens per minute to simulate a mid-tier load. we'll do controlled ramp ups.
[04:26] Miguel Santos: we can provide the traffic generator and a sample of logs.
[04:29] Marcus Li: perfect. also we'll instrument for tail lat and cold start behavior — the KV cache warmups matter for chat use cases.
[04:40] Liam O'Connor: any data residency concerns? we're EU and US tenants; want specific region pinning.
[04:47] Priya Patel: region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted can be pinned to region endpoints where available. we'll note region in the runbook.
[04:56] Alicia Park: pricing — high-level, what are the obvious trade-offs?
[04:59] Priya Patel: hosted is fastest to start but variable cost, dedicated is capex-like monthly commits with predictable throughput and lower per-token unit price. we'll put a matrix in the follow-up with sample numbers based on your expected QPS.
[05:11] Marcus Li: quick tech caveat — if you need sub-100ms tail latency at scale, the choice of kernels and model variants matters; we'll propose a few model profiles that match your prompt lengths.
[05:23] Miguel Santos: any blockers on our side for initial onboarding?
[05:26] Jordan Nguyen: we need SSO metadata, an initial list of service accounts, and the sample traffic profile. after that we can queue the staging benchmark.
[05:36] Nora Chen: we should also discuss who the day-to-day contacts are for incidents during pilot.
[05:40] Alicia Park: it's me for product, Miguel for infra, Liam for security.
[05:44] Priya Patel: perfect, we'll add those contacts to the runbook.
[05:48] Marcus Li: I'll put together a proposed test plan and a checklist for the staging session.
[05:53] Miguel Santos: one more question — do you support API gateway rewriting rules for path-based routing? we use an API gateway that prefers header-based tenant routing.
[06:02] Marcus Li: yes, we can support header-based routing and token scoping; we also support path-based mapping. we might need a small adaptor if your gateway enforces mTLS; we can provide the adaptor sample.
[06:15] Liam O'Connor: regarding S S O, we'll send SAML metadata, but prefer SCIM for user provisioning later. does Redwood support SCIM?
[06:24] Jordan Nguyen: yes, SCIM provisioning is supported, we'll include the SCIM endpoint docs.
[06:28] Priya Patel: ok, to recap next steps: we'll send the connectivity checklist and the SOC2 + SSO docs, Marcus will propose the benchmark plan and run a baseline, Jordan will attach compliance docs to the CRM and start the pilot paperwork. CobaltWorks will share traffic profile and SSO metadata.
[06:45] Alicia Park: sounds good. can you share the docs in the shared drive and flag if any of the items are blockers?
[06:51] Priya Patel: yes, we'll post a single link to the drive and include a short priority flag.
[06:55] Miguel Santos: thanks, talk soon.
[06:58] Priya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items and propose times for the benchmark.

(End of recording — remaining time used for quick sync about calendar invites and internal notes)
